body: Multi-agent LLM pipelines are often credited with gains in software engineering tasks, but it is rarely clear whether a gain stems from the typed contract between agents or from the specialized prompts that decomposition enables. We study this attribution problem in Requirements Engineering, comparing three architectures for classifying requirements as functional or non-functional and then prioritizing them with MoSCoW: a single-call baseline; a two-call variant that reuses the pipeline's specialized prompts but passes an unvalidated intermediate; and a pipeline with a Pydantic-validated typed state. The 18 conditions cover PROMISE NFR+ (625 requirements), three locally hosted small language models, and two languages. The F1 gain over the baseline is associated with the two-call, specialized-prompt variant (up to +0.075), whereas the typed state adds a small difference (-0.003 to +0.013) that is significant in one of six comparisons. Beyond accuracy, the typed pipeline contains out-of-range model outputs at the agent boundary, while the unvalidated variant fails later and drops the requirement, and it shows a small, reproducible increase in inter-model MoSCoW consistency whose cause our design cannot isolate. The study is associative: the contrasts bundle prompts, call count, and staged context, and the results come from three 7--8B models on one dataset. The implementation and replication package are archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23380444).
summaryZh: 超越准确性：在多代理 LLM 管道中将分解与类型化状态质量保证分开。多代理 LLM 管道通常被认为在软件工程任务中带来了收益，但很少清楚这种收益是源于代理之间的类型化合同，还是源于分解所带来的专门提示。我们在需求工程中研究了这个归因问题，比较了将需求分类为功能性或非功能性的三种架构，然后使用 MoSCoW 对它们进行优先级排序：两次调用变体，重用管道的专门提示，但传递未经验证的中间体；以及具有 Pydantic 验证的类型化状态的管道。
